existing_programs: Plasma-cell adhesion molecule; described as a T-cell recognition target in adult T-cell leukemia; less developed in MM specifically.

none known — no CCND1-directed vaccine, CAR-T, ADC or bispecific in myeloma that I can name with confidence; CCND1 peptide/CTL work exists preclinically (mantle cell lymphoma, breast cancer) but I am not aware of a registered clinical vaccine trial, so I am not claiming tier 1a/1b

none known as a CD1D-directed peptide vaccine or CD1D-targeting agent. Note: alpha-galactosylceramide (KRN7000)-loaded dendritic cell / iNKT trials in MGUS-SMM-MM (e.g., Richter et al., Blood 2013; Chang/Dhodapkar studies) exploit CD1d as the lipid-presenting molecule, not as the targeted tumor antigen, so this does not constitute a CD1D-directed clinical program.
Samalizumab (anti-CD200 mAb) trialed in MM; CD200-CD200R axis is an established immune-evasion checkpoint in MM; CAR/bispecific interest.
CKS1B (paralog) is the well-known 1q21 MM amplicon driver; CKS2 less established in MM.
Retinaldehyde dehydrogenase in antigen-presenting cells; no MM programs.
pUMVC3-hDKK1 DNA vaccine in smouldering myeloma (Mayo Clinic, NCT03591614); also anti-DKK1 mAb BHQ880 (Novartis) in MM phase 1b/2 trials, and DKN-01 in other solid tumours
Endothelin-B receptor; endothelin axis in MM bone disease; ET receptor antagonists exist clinically (pulmonary hypertension).
none known for FCRLA itself; note the paralogue FCRL5/FcRH5 is clinically validated in MM (cevostamab, BFCR4350A; anti-FcRH5 ADC DFRF4539A; FcRH5 CAR-T), but that is a different gene
Secreted Wnt antagonist implicated in MM bone disease; no direct therapeutic programs.

Rilotumumab (AMG 102), an anti-HGF neutralising monoclonal antibody, was evaluated in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (phase 1/2, alone and with bortezomib); HGF/MET axis also targeted by ficlatuzumab and MET TKIs in other tumours. No HGF peptide vaccine in MM.

none known for IGF1 itself as a vaccine target; the axis has been drugged in MM via the receptor (anti-IGF-1R antibodies AVE1642 and figitumumab/CP-751,871 in phase I myeloma studies) and the ligand neutralised in solid tumours (xentuzumab/BI 836845), but no IGF1-directed vaccine or MM ligand-targeted program exists

none known as an antigen-directed agent in myeloma; KIT is targeted pharmacologically by TKIs (imatinib/dasatinib, tested in MM without antigen-specific rationale) and anti-CD117 antibodies (e.g. briquilimab/JSP191) and CD117 CAR-T are in development for AML/HSC conditioning, not myeloma
Hematopoietic lysosomal protein; no MM-specific programs known.
Neuronal adhesion; deletions in some cancers.

none known - no vaccine, CAR, antibody or ADC program against MX1 in myeloma or any other indication that I am aware of; MX1 appears in myeloma literature only as a component of type I interferon-response gene signatures, not as a therapeutic target
CD56 is a classic MM surface marker (esp. t(11;14)); lorvotuzumab mertansine (anti-NCAM1 ADC) trialed in MM; CAR-NK/CAR-T programs exist.
Giant muscle structural protein; none relevant.
Glutamine transporter; CAR-T target in AML; metabolic therapy interest.
none known in myeloma; anti-CD43 antibody AT1413 has been explored in AML (not myeloma, not a vaccine), and CD43 CAR constructs remain preclinical
Plasma-cell sialyltransferase; ST3GAL6-MMP1 axis described in MM cell migration; no therapeutic programs.
STING agonists have been evaluated in cancer immunotherapy including myeloma models, but as adjuvants that engage the pathway, not as antigens
TRAIL receptor agonists trialed in cancer.
